text.p: Gillette Co said it was planning to launch a new advertisement targetting men who use disposable razors, challenging them to try the company's Sensor refillable razor system.
The company said its ad would challenge disposable users in print, radio and television spots scheduled to air later this month.

Peter Hoffman, senior vice president of Gillette's North Atlantic division, said the company has 80 percent of the market for refillable razors. But 40 percent of all shavers still use disposable, he said, so the advertisements are focused on the "unconverted" rather than rivals in the refillable category.
He said ths company would spend about $80 million in 1997 for Sensor advertising.

The company also is releasing in early 1997 about $35 million worth of advertisements for its Gillette and Right Guard clear stick anti-perspirants as well as its Soft & Dri Silken Solid anti-perspirant for women.
